Three drops in this song and each has to be bigger than the last, or the second reads as the show losing interest.

Voice and almost nothing else. The outer pair holds a very low blue bed; the inner pair is not here -- it belongs to the singer (see the binding). The head is a still white pin. Nothing moves that the song has not moved.
9.11s, the score's 'drums thicken' moment: the whole row comes into the bed, a little brighter. Still blue, still still.
17.75s: the tempo lifts from 89 to 119 and the song starts to walk. The room starts to walk with it -- a slow blue pulse on the new beat. The first rhythm the row has shown.

The voice at its loudest before the riff: the OUTER pair now follows it (binding) and the inner pair holds low, the reverse of the opening -- the same idea, turned round, so the section reads as new without spending anything.
A low blue bed under the exchange; the picture here is the binding.

The loudest twelve seconds on the record: the two pairs call and respond on EVERY beat, red and WHITE. White is a hit, and here the song hits on every beat, so the row does -- which makes this both the brightest and the busiest stretch of the show, where it belongs. The head is white with the prism; the four hardest kicks get a white strobe on top.

A quiet blue bed under the colour wave and nothing else. The wave had been sitting on the drop's red/blue frame and the two blended into a grey near-white -- the brightest thing in the show by accident, and the travel unreadable. A wave needs a still field to cross.

The inner pair breathes with the SINGER: every sung phrase swells the two middle lamps, in blue, and they fall away between phrases. The room is doing what the voice is doing, which is the difference between quiet and bland.
Before the riff the voice is at its loudest, so the OUTER pair follows it now -- the opening's figure turned round.

THE TWO HALVES ARGUING. This is where the song is a call and response between the lead voice and the answering voices, so the left pair follows the lead in blue and the right pair follows the answer in red -- the room literally takes sides. New picture for a new section, and the only place it is used.

gestures.why: The head is a still white pin on the left wall, low, for the whole opening. It does not move. Its first movement will be an event because of these fourteen seconds.
13.83s: synth and backing voices enter -- the strongest moment in the intro. One beat of white across the row, the first hit of the show.
And the head's FIRST movement: one glide from the left wall to the right, on the entrance, then still again. One move in half a minute, so it is seen.

THE BASS RIFF. Bass and strings, no drums, no voice: the one fixture that can point becomes the soloist. Clean white beam, no prism, snapping to a new wall on every downbeat -- four bars, four places -- and drifting across each bar with the bass. The row stays a dim blue field underneath so the beam cuts. Now: it NODS hard and FLASHES on beats 2 and 2-and-a-half, where the riff punches, from the very first bar -- and each turn to a new wall begins a beat early so the head arrives on the downbeat instead of leaving on it.

33.75s: bass and strings arrive together out of a one-second black. ONE beat of the whole row in white -- the row's single big statement in this phrase -- and then it drops to the blue bed and the head takes over. This was the biggest arrival in the first half of the song and it had been getting a dim bed fading in.

Bar 15: the red spark leaves on beat 2 and ARRIVES on the 'and' of 2 -- which is where this riff actually punches, every bar. A run is read when it lands, not when it starts, so it is aimed to land on the hit and takes a quarter of a second, not a whole beat. Left to right.

Bar 22, the C-major lift before the drop: the row at FULL in violet -- as far toward red as the build ever gets -- for two beats. Held at 0.85, not full: the last bar of the build was the brightest two seconds in the whole show, and the drop has to be bigger than the thing that led into it. Then NOTHING for two beats, head included. Eight bars of the room warming and moving, and it stops dead. This silence is what makes the next beat enormous.
49.75s, THE DROP. Every lamp to full WHITE for one beat, snapped, no fade. The room has been blue for fifty seconds; this is the first white and the drums arriving.

The head goes RED with the PRISM for the first time all night: one red beam becomes six red rays, snapping wall to wall on every beat over a row that is now red and blue. The prism was withheld for fifty seconds so that this reads as an arrival. The prism PULSES on the front of every beat rather than sitting on, the tilt kicks on every beat, and each turn leaves a beat early so it lands on the beat.
52.76s: the whole band at full strength, six families at once. One full BEAT of white across the row, held, not an 80ms flash -- the head keeps snapping red underneath it.

BAR 30. The drums fall out completely across this bar (kick 0.47 -> 0.04 -> 0.00) before the second drop. White flashes take their place: quick, seemingly random, accelerating across the row for three beats -- the transition move. The 240ms hole at 64.20 stays as a stutter inside them.
The head joins the acceleration: dead centre, white, no prism, strobing on every beat -- the first time the head has flashed white since the riff. Then the beat of black at 65.25, then red.

A genuine 200ms hole at 64.2s: the band falls to under half its own level right here, just before the drums come back full. Black for exactly as long as the hole, so the room breathes with the track instead of over it.
One beat of nothing before the drums come back full at bar 31.
Bar 31 lands. The build was kept cold on purpose so this is the first white the room sees.

Third drop: the head's move a third time, escalated once more -- red, prism, and now strobing on EVERY beat, not just the downbeat. Same figure each drop, bigger each time, so the room learns it and then feels it grow.

THE COLOUR WAVE as this section's identity: the row stays lit in blue and a RED position walks across it, twice a bar, turning each bar. Only the hue moves. Red over blue, not white over red: white is a hit in this show and a white wave here outshone the loudest section that follows. Peak 0.85: this is a RESOLVE, and it sits under the climax that follows, not over it.

Two beats of nothing before the loudest kick in the song. Everything stops -- and this is the one place in the record where the whole band is already at full, so the hole is the loudest thing in the room.

THE LOUDEST KICK IN THE SONG at 102.76s -- full strength in the kick lane, the top of four consecutive bars that hold the four hardest hits on the record. Whole rig, full white, held for three beats. This is the peak of the show and it is placed on the hit rather than on a bar line. Four beats: this is the loudest kick in the song and the show's brightest moment lives here, not in the build.
